message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on North Carolina Avenue in this auction.

I have a pink monopoly with four houses on each property. The opponent has a dark blue monopoly with heavy development. I have $726 cash and one get-out-of-jail card.

p3 is bankrupt. p4 has a light blue monopoly with four houses and $763 cash, but is in jail. The auction for North Carolina Avenue is at $123, requiring a $124 minimum bid.

Bidding $124 for North Carolina Avenue would net $26 cash after mortgaging the property, since its mortgage value is $150. This would also deny p4 a second green property.

p4 already owns Pennsylvania Avenue, while p1 holds Pacific Avenue. If I win the auction, the greens would be split three ways and no player could form a green monopoly without trading. p1 is cash-poor but still holds a dark blue monopoly, so they might trade Pacific to p4 to complete it.

I am calculating the rent for Park Place with three houses at $1100 and Boardwalk with four houses at $1700. These are the next spaces after Pennsylvania Avenue.

p1 landed on North Carolina Avenue and is now auctioning it. I will bid $124, staying under my $150 cap. I am weighing whether to drop out or raise further.

p4 has been matching every bid by one dollar and appears willing to raise further. I will continue bidding in one-dollar increments until I reach my $150 cap, then drop out. A mortgaged North Carolina Avenue would cost $165 to unmortgage, but blocking p4 from completing a second green is worth the investment.

Mortgaging the property after winning would leave me with $752 cash, which is better than my current $726. Without mortgaging, the property would sit idle as a dead asset. I am also weighing the risk of landing on Park Place or Boardwalk next turn, since those spaces are two and four spaces away from Pennsylvania Avenue.

p4's light blue properties are expensive to develop, but they are less immediately lethal than a dark blue monopoly. My pink properties with four houses are even more costly to attack. This makes the green auction a strategic priority.
